calendar_extra: Next week: Thanksgiving Day, a Federal Reserve holiday. Check your bank's holiday cutoffs for payments dated around it.
deck: Treasury yields rose on the week, bills included, while SOFR barely moved. Thanksgiving falls next week.
read: The Federal Reserve held its policy rate at 3.75–4.00% on October 28, with two of twelve voters preferring a quarter-point increase. Overnight funding is steady: SOFR was 3.90% and the effective federal funds rate 3.88% on Thursday, November 12, and the SOFR 30-day average was 3.92% on Friday. The prime rate is 7.00%.

Treasury yields rose on the week. The 2-year closed Friday at 4.88%, 37 bp above November 6, and the 10-year at 5.15%, 29 bp higher. The largest daily move came on Tuesday, November 10, when the 2-year rose 17 bp; October consumer prices were released that morning, up 0.4% on the month and 0.3% excluding food and energy. Bills rose too: the 1-month bill is at 4.10% and the 6-month at 4.42%.

For a company, the week split two ways. SOFR, where most floating-rate credit lines reset, was almost unchanged, while the Treasury yields that fixed-rate loans and bonds are priced from rose by about a third of a point. Short-term cash earns a little more than a week ago. The minutes of the October FOMC meeting are due Wednesday at 2:00 p.m. ET.
cash: Each 0.25 point on $10 million of SOFR- or prime-based borrowing is $25,000 a year in interest, before any floor or hedge. The SOFR 30-day average was 3.92% on Friday, within a basis point of a week earlier.
Every 1 point of yield on $5 million of idle cash is $50,000 a year. Compare your account’s rate, after fees and earnings credits, with the 4.10% one-month bill.
Thursday, November 26 is a Federal Reserve holiday. Check payroll, vendor runs and debt payments dated around it against your bank’s holiday cutoffs.
